First, recall the following:

- ${J}_{2}(-4)$ represents a $2\times 2$ Jordan block with $-4$'s on the leading diagonal.

- ${J}_{1}(6)$ represents a $1\times 1$ Jordan block with $6$'s on the leading diagonal,

Therefore, our Jordan blocks are given by

$$
{J}_{2}(-4)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}],\,{J}_{1}(6)=[\begin{aligned}6\end{aligned}].
$$

The composition of our Jordan blocks gives the following block diagonal matrix:

$$
{J}_{2}(-4)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(6)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$
